steps.body: Converting length runs both ways: meters to centimeters multiplies by 100, and centimeters to meters divides by it.
steps.narration: Converting length runs both ways: meters to centimeters multiplies by 100, and centimeters to meters divides by it.

widget.prompt: How many centimeters in 4 meters? Hop one meter at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Three hops reach 300 cm; the object is four meters long.
Five hops overshoot — four meters is 400 centimeters.

widget.missFeedback: Four meters needs four hops of 100 centimeters.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — four meters needs four hops of 100 centimeters.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — four meters stops exactly at 400 centimeters.

cml.actionGoal: Choose multiplication or division from the direction of a metric length conversion.
invariants: Meters to centimeters multiplies by 100; centimeters to meters divides by 100.
misconceptions: Using the right factor in the wrong direction.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A route measures 7 kilometers, and each kilometer is 1000 meters. Compute 7 × 1000.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding mixes a quantity with a rate. Each of the 7 kilometers contributes 1000 meters, so they multiply.
That divided. Going to the SMALLER unit needs more of them, so the number must grow.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the quantity and the conversion factor, then decide whether the count should grow or shrink.

steps.body: Decide the direction before you compute. Going to the smaller unit the number grows; going to the bigger unit it shrinks.
steps.narration: Decide the direction before you compute. Going to the smaller unit the number grows; going to the bigger unit it shrinks.

widget.prompt: Apply the length relationship to a new value: how many centimeters are in 6 meters?

commonLandings.feedback: Five hops reach 500 centimeters; six meters needs one more hop.
Seven hops overshoot; six meters is 600 centimeters.

widget.missFeedback: Six equal hops of 100 centimeters land at 600 centimeters.
widget.successFeedback: 600 centimeters — six meter-hops of 100 centimeters each.
widget.lowFeedback: This landing is short of six complete meter-hops.
widget.highFeedback: This landing is past six complete meter-hops.

widget.prompt: Apply without the opening model: A trail measures 700 centimeters, and each meter is 100 centimeters. Compute 700 ÷ 100.

commonErrors.feedback: 700 is the count in centimeters. Switching to the bigger meter must make the NUMBER smaller.
That multiplied. Going to the BIGGER unit needs fewer of them, so divide.

widget.prompt: Retrieve or diagnose in a new form: Converting 5 kilograms into grams, do you multiply or divide by 1,000?

options.label: Multiply — grams are smaller, so there are more of them
options.feedback: Correct — each kilogram contains 1,000 grams, so 5 kilograms is 5,000 grams.

options.label: Divide — the number should get smaller
options.feedback: Dividing would give 0.005, which is far less than the mass you started with.

options.label: Neither — the number stays the same
options.feedback: The mass stays the same, but the NUMBER must change because the unit changed.

options.label: Multiply by 100
options.feedback: 100 is the centimeters-per-meter factor; a kilogram holds 1,000 grams.

widget.prompt: A trail measures 4000 meters, and each kilometer is 1000 meters. Compute 4000 ÷ 1000.

commonErrors.feedback: That multiplied. Kilometers are the BIGGER unit, so fewer of them are needed — divide instead.
Subtracting removes a fixed amount once; converting to a bigger unit divides the whole count by 1000.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Decide whether the target unit is bigger or smaller, then multiply or divide by the stated factor.
